sub7: Not a search — a bounded retime of a design that already existed, with every figure computed from the cells
method:
1 · Three cells, and the reason there are only three. The parent design was measured hour by hour against the December demand curve and the misfit was not spread evenly — Sunday carried half of it on its own. So rather than re-search the link, each individual cell was tested against every retime of ±4 hours, and the best was taken, three times over. The moves are: line 21 Sunday 13:30–22:00 → 14:55–23:25, line 8 Saturday 13:30–21:00 → 11:00–18:30, and line 20 Sunday 08:30–16:30 → 07:15–15:15. Nothing else in the 168 cells differs from the parent.

2 · Why nothing else could move. Every retime keeps the duty's length to the minute. That is not a convention observed carefully — it is what makes the Monday-to-Saturday total, every line's 35h, both headcounts, the four cover weeks and the longest worked run impossible to change, rather than merely unchanged. The search was also refused any move that took the tightest rest in the whole design below 12h30, or that moved the day's open or close, or that produced a :05 or :10 time.

3 · Where it stops. A fourth move was available and was rejected: it bought 2.6 points of fit by taking Sunday's open back from four people to three — giving back the December rule the third move had just met. This is a bounded improvement to somebody else's design, not a recommendation, and it carries all of the parent's class-C caveats unchanged.

intro2:
This is not a new link. It is “Clean Final” with three cells retimed, and the point of it is the size of the change: three cells out of 168, three people's single days, against a demand misfit cut by a fifth.

Measured against the December curve the way every proposal here is measured — the squared gap between each hour's share of demand and its share of cover, lower being better — the parent's seven days score Mon 28.4 · Tue 43.6 · Wed 42.3 · Thu 48.8 · Fri 31.0 · Sat 28.5 · Sun 62.4. The three moves touch Saturday, which falls to 20.5, and Sunday, which falls to 44.9 — each a 28% improvement. The five weekdays are not touched and score exactly as before. The Wk fit column opposite is the fit of the average weekday, so it reads the same for this design and its parent — no weekday cell moved; page 4 carries each day's own figure.
dutyNote: Why the duties land where they do: Monday to Saturday totals exactly 42,000 minutes — 20 × 35h to the minute — and it could not have come out otherwise, because all three moves preserve duty length. The daily split is the parent's, unchanged: Mon 6,225 · Tue 7,205 · Wed 7,205 · Thu 7,780 · Fri 7,690 · Sat 5,895 minutes. Saturday is still the lightest day and Thursday the heaviest, a spread of nearly two duties — that question belongs to the parent and is not answered here. What DID change is where two of Sunday's nine people and one of Saturday's twelve stand in the day, and the coverage rows opposite show it.
openQuestions: Sunday now closes with four, where the shape asks three. This is the one December rule the three moves BREAK, and it is worth arguing rather than fixing: 22:00 was Sunday's deepest shortfall in the parent, so the rule and the measured demand disagree here and the move sides with the demand. If the rule wins, drop the first move — and Sunday goes back to 62.4. Sunday now opens with four, which is the rule met, where the parent opened with three. That is the third move, and it is why a fourth was refused: the best fourth move available took it straight back to three for 2.6 points of fit. One rest gets tighter. Line 8 works Friday 14:00–22:30; its Saturday moving to 11:00 cuts that turnaround from 15h00 to 12h30 — the tightest rest anywhere here, half an hour above the 12h floor. An 11:30 start would hold 13h00 and give back 2.7 points of Saturday fit. That is the only one of the three moves that costs anybody anything. Thursday is now the worst-fitting day in the design, at 48.8. Nothing here addresses it: it is also the heaviest day by minutes (7,780 against Monday's 6,225), and the two facts are the same fact. That is the next question, and it is a weekday-table question rather than a three-cell one. Everything else the parent did not answer, it still does not. Saturday opens with five and closes with three against four and four; Saturday carries 12 people against 14 and Sunday 9 against 10; 4.35 days a week against 4.2; the longest late is 8h40 against a longest early of 8h30; five December movements fall after Sunday's 23:25 finish. None of these moved, because none is a question three retimes can answer.
